                 SENATOR JOHN R. KUHL, JR., Acting President

                           P R O C E E D I N G S

                 Senate will come to order.  I ask the members

                 to take their places, staff to take their

                 places.

                            And if everyone will please rise

                 and repeat with me the Pledge of Allegiance.

                            (Whereupon, the assemblage recited

                 the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.)

                            ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:    In the

                 absence of clergy, may we bow our heads in a

                 moment of silence.

                            (Whereupon, the assemblage

                 respected a moment of silence.)

                            ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:    Senator

                 Bruno, I have at the desk here a proclamation

                 which I'm handing down to the Secretary at

                 this time.

                 President.

                            ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:    I ask the

                 Secretary to read it in its entirety.

                            THE SECRETARY:    "Proclamation:

                            "Pursuant to the power vested in me

                 by Article 4, Section 3 of the Constitution, I







                                                        3



                 hereby convene the Legislature in

                 Extraordinary Session at the Capitol, in the

                 City of Albany, on the 17th day of September,

                 2001, at 10:00 o'clock in the morning, for the

                 purpose of considering legislation I will

                 submit with respect to creating criminal

                 offenses for persons who commit or support

                 terrorist acts or harbor or otherwise assist

                 persons who commit terrorist acts, enhancing

                 criminal penalties for those who threaten to

                 place a bomb in any public or private place,

                 and creating an emergency management

                 assistance compact, and for the consideration

                 of legislation with respect to such other

                 subjects as I may recommend.

                            "Given under my hand and the privy

                 seal of the State, in the City of New York

                 this 16th day of September in the year 2001,

                 George E. Pataki, Governor."

                 proclamation having been read, the session is

                 in extraordinary session.

                 the Secretary to read.

                            ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:    Senator

                 Duane, why do you rise?

                            SENATOR DUANE:    Thank you, Mr.

                 President.  I just -- was that the message of

                 necessity for the bill, or was that the actual

                 bill?

                            ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:    We passed

                 two bills, Senator Duane.

                            SENATOR DUANE:    If I may speak on

                 the second bill, Mr. President, I want to

                 explain my vote.

                            ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:    Senator

                 Duane, to explain his vote on Calendar

                 Number 2.

                            SENATOR DUANE:    Thank you very

                 much, Mr. President.

                            I first want to put my vote into

                 context here.  And I want to praise as highly

                 and greatly as I possibly can the wonderful

                 efforts of the Mayor of the City of New York,

                 Mayor Giuliani, and our Governor, and the







                                                        19



                 quick and decisive action they've taken to

                 help our city and our constituents.

                            The events of the past week have

                 been one of the most tragic chapters in this

                 state's history.  I'm angered and I'm also

                 saddened, as an American and as a New Yorker,

                 and as a State Senator from the 27th District,

                 the district of TriBeCa, Battery Park City,

                 the Trade Center, the downtown Manhattan area

                 that I share with Senator Connor and Speaker

                 Silver and my colleague Assembly Member Glick.

                            The loss and destruction caused by

                 last Tuesday's attacks has really crippled my

                 district.  I've spent the last week talking to

                 those on the front lines, in fire stations,

                 EMS, police precincts, all of whom have been

                 devastated by the tremendous loss of life.

                 They were on the front lines and the first to

                 go to the Trade Center.

                            Large numbers of my constituents

                 are missing loved ones.  Residents have been

                 forced out of their homes.  Businesses have

                 shut down.  The air near the attack is filled

                 with who knows what horrible contaminants,

                 maybe even asbestos, other harmful air which







                                                        20



                 children were forced to breathe.  I breathed

                 in that air myself.

                            I mean, the loss and destruction to

                 my district is staggering.  I've seen what

                 weapons of mass destruction can do, what it

                 did to the World Trade Center, Battery Park

                 City, TriBeCa.  Father Mychal Judge was a good

                 friend of mine, and I loved him very much.

                 And his death is a great loss to all of us.

                 Our public schools are destroyed.

                            And I believe that these evil acts

                 should be severely punished.  However, after

                 much thought and deliberation, I feel

                 compelled to vote against this measure today.

                 As many of you know, I am against the death

                 penalty, and this bill contains a new category

                 for capital punishment.

                            I also believe that the

                 responsibility of punishing those who would

                 dare use a weapon of mass destruction lies

                 with the federal government.  And in fact, the

                 federal government already has laws in place

                 which would bring the death penalty to those

                 who utilize weapons of mass destruction.

                            These are the reasons that I've







                                                        21



                 voted against this -- against similar bills in

                 the past and why I'm voting against it today

                 as well.

                            I will fight, though, to ensure

                 that we do all we can to ease the suffering of

                 New Yorkers.  And in the weeks ahead I urge

                 that we continue to come here to pass measures

                 which achieve this goal.

                            And again, I want to commend the

                 governor and the mayor, police, fire, EMS, all

                 the volunteers, the construction workers, for

                 their tireless efforts in this time of crisis,

                 and to all of the people of New York State for

                 coming together to help us.

                            Thank you, Mr. President.

                            ACTING PRESIDENT KUHL:    Senator
